Dodge Debuts the Sub-Zero Paint for Its Durango Bestseller
7 photos
Photo: Dodge
Dodge has just debuted the Sub-Zero paint in the Durango lineup eight months after introducing it for the Charger two-door and four-door, both ICE and EV. It is the 11th exterior option that customers can choose from when they spec their future Durango SUV with a HEMI under the hood.
Sub-Zero drops as a solid blue-gray exterior finish, formulated specifically to deliver two distinct visual personalities based on how the light strikes, Dodge reps explain. The paint appears deep and subtle in the shade, but it is a brighter, cool-tone blue in direct sunlight.
The color debuted on the all-new 2 026 Dodge Charger back in March, becoming available for the entire lineup, regardless of the number of doors or powertrain. Eight months later, it was ported into the Durango lineup as Dodge is trying to make its aging SUV more attractive. The third generation of the third-row SUV has been on the market since 2010, when it was launched as a 2011 model year.
The introduction of Sub-Zero expands the configuration possibilities of the flagship Durango SRT Hellcat Jailbreak. Dodge confirms that adding this eleventh paint tone officially unlocks more than 22 million unique potential configurations from the factory.
Photo: Dodge Jailbreak buyers ordering a Sub-Zero Durango can mix and match a massive factory catalog. They can go for matte-finish tinted dual stripes, five distinct brake caliper colors, and a generous list of fatory wheel designs, including the returning bronze Brass Monkey package.
In the meantime, Dodge offers custom interior leather options, such as Petrol Blue or Red stitching, exclusive materials, and custom badging combinations, so you’ll rarely see two Dodge Durango Jailbreak-customized models that look alike.
The arrival of the Sub-Zero marks the fourth consecutive month that Dodge has introduced a new factory color for the Durango. Dodge brought the Redeye in August and the After Dark in September. October was the month of the stealthy matte Smokescreen, while November has just delivered the Sub-Zero.
These four new entries bring the total 2027 model-year exterior lineup to 11 distinct paint options. The other remaining colors anchoring the lineup are B5 Blue, Destroyer Grey, Green Machine, Night Moves, Pitch Black, Red Oxide, and White Knuckle.
Photo: Dodge Unlike the Charger, where the new Sub-Zero demands a $795 premium over MSRP, ordering the new paint on the 2027 Durango costs $595 across the entire lineup. The paint is already available for all the HEMI-powered Durangos.
This means that it can become an option for those who want to go home with the Durango powered by the 5.7-liter HEMI V8, the 6.4-liter HEMI V8, or the almighty 6.2-liter supercharged HEMI V8, which cranks out 710 horsepower (720 metric horsepower). The HEMI lineup starts at $43,675. The SRT Jailbreak Hellcat is an $80,990 deal.
Last year, the aging Dodge Durango single-handedly carried the brand on its shoulders, accounting for nearly 80% of all Dodge vehicles sold nationwide. In fact, the Durango posted its best individual sales year since 2005, despite the automaker’s figures dropping by 28% compared to 2024.
Dodge sold 81,168 Durangos in 2025, with the Hornet coming in second with only 9,365. The electric Dodge Charger Daytona rounded out the podium with 7,421 units moved last year. This year, things haven’t changed much for the Durango, which was selected by 61,330 customers from January to September.
